Every error that GreenLens reports has a stable code, a one-line message, the cause and a suggested fix. Text in braces is replaced with the actual values, such as the name of the command.

## GL0001

- **Message:** unexpected internal error
- **Cause:** `{detail}`
- **Fix:** report it at https://github.com/MarioUrenaGarcia/greenlens/issues with the output of 'greenlens version'
- **Exit code:** 1

## GL0002

- **Message:** unknown command '`{command}`'
- **Cause:** '`{command}`' is not a command of '`{parent}`'
- **Fix:** run '`{parent}` --help' to list the available commands
- **Exit code:** 2

## GL0003

- **Message:** unknown flag '`{flag}`'
- **Cause:** '`{command}`' does not accept the flag '`{flag}`'
- **Fix:** run '`{command}` --help' to list the accepted flags
- **Exit code:** 2

## GL0004

- **Message:** flag '`{flag}`' needs a value
- **Cause:** the flag was given without a value
- **Fix:** pass a value after the flag, for example '`{flag}` &lt;value&gt;'
- **Exit code:** 2

## GL0005

- **Message:** invalid value '`{value}`' for flag '`{flag}`'
- **Cause:** the value does not have the type that '`{flag}`' expects
- **Fix:** run '`{command}` --help' to see the accepted values
- **Exit code:** 2

## GL0006

- **Message:** invalid flag syntax '`{arg}`'
- **Cause:** a flag starts with '-' followed by one letter, or '--' followed by a name
- **Fix:** run '`{command}` --help' to see how to write each flag
- **Exit code:** 2

## GL0007

- **Message:** '`{command}`' does not accept arguments
- **Cause:** received: `{args}`
- **Fix:** run '`{command}` --help' to see how to use it
- **Exit code:** 2

## GL0008

- **Message:** unsupported language '`{lang}`'
- **Cause:** the language comes from `{source}`
- **Fix:** use one of: `{supported}`
- **Exit code:** 2

## GL0009

- **Message:** unsupported output format '`{value}`'
- **Cause:** the output can be written only as `{formats}`
- **Fix:** pass one of these to --output
- **Exit code:** 2

## GL0010

- **Message:** unknown error code '`{code}`'
- **Cause:** `{code}` is not an error code of GreenLens
- **Fix:** see the error code reference in the documentation
- **Exit code:** 2

## GL0011

- **Message:** cannot start '`{command}`'
- **Cause:** `{detail}`
- **Fix:** check the name of the command and that it is in PATH
- **Exit code:** 1

## GL0012

- **Message:** measure needs exactly one target
- **Cause:** give a command after --, or --pid, or --unit, but only one of them
- **Fix:** run 'greenlens measure --help' for examples
- **Exit code:** 2

## GL0013

- **Message:** process `{pid}` does not exist
- **Cause:** no process has that PID, or it is not visible from here
- **Fix:** check the PID with ps, or measure a command instead
- **Exit code:** 1

## GL0014

- **Message:** cannot find the cgroup of `{unit}`
- **Cause:** no cgroup v2 directory named `{unit}` exists under /sys/fs/cgroup
- **Fix:** check the name with 'systemctl status', and that the unit is running
- **Exit code:** 1

## GL1001

- **Message:** no measured energy source is available
- **Cause:** this machine exposes no readable energy counter, as in most virtual machines
- **Fix:** run 'greenlens doctor' to see which sources were found and how to enable them
- **Exit code:** 3

## GL1002

- **Message:** cannot read RAPL energy counters
- **Cause:** `{path}` is readable only by root
- **Fix:** run 'sudo greenlens setup-permissions' or see 'greenlens help GL1002'
- **Exit code:** 5

## GL1003

- **Message:** cannot open the perf_event energy counters
- **Cause:** system-wide perf events need perf_event_paranoid 0 or less, or CAP_PERFMON (perf_event_paranoid is `{paranoid}`)
- **Fix:** run 'sudo greenlens setup-permissions --perfmon', or rely on the powercap counters
- **Exit code:** 5

## GL1004

- **Message:** cannot open the IPMI device
- **Cause:** `{path}` is not accessible to this user
- **Fix:** run 'sudo greenlens setup-permissions --ipmi'
- **Exit code:** 5

## GL1005

- **Message:** cannot read a hwmon power sensor
- **Cause:** `{path}` is not readable by this user
- **Fix:** run 'sudo greenlens setup-permissions' or check the permissions of the sensor
- **Exit code:** 5

## GL1006

- **Message:** the BMC does not report power readings
- **Cause:** the DCMI power reading command returned `{detail}`
- **Fix:** enable power monitoring in the BMC settings, or use another platform source
- **Exit code:** 3

## GL1007

- **Message:** CPU energy is estimated
- **Cause:** no energy counter of the processor is readable on this machine
- **Fix:** on bare metal run 'sudo greenlens setup-permissions'; in a virtual machine set sources.estimate in the configuration
- **Exit code:** 3

## GL1008

- **Message:** an energy counter can wrap more than once between samples
- **Cause:** `{channel}` wraps after `{range}`, which takes `{period}` at the highest power seen, and the sampling interval is `{interval}`
- **Fix:** set agent.sample_interval below `{limit}`
- **Exit code:** 1

## GL1009

- **Message:** power sensor of an unknown hwmon driver is not used
- **Cause:** hwmon device '`{name}`' reports power or energy, but its domain is not known
- **Fix:** report the driver name at https://github.com/MarioUrenaGarcia/greenlens/issues so it can be classified
- **Exit code:** 3

## GL1010

- **Message:** the processor is not in the estimation table
- **Cause:** '`{model}`' has no published power coefficients, so a generic average per thread is used
- **Fix:** set sources.estimate.idle_watts and sources.estimate.full_watts in the configuration with values for this processor
- **Exit code:** 3

## GL1011

- **Message:** changing permissions needs root
- **Cause:** the command runs as `{user}`
- **Fix:** run 'sudo greenlens setup-permissions --apply'
- **Exit code:** 5

## GL1012

- **Message:** step `{step}` of the plan failed
- **Cause:** `{detail}`
- **Fix:** fix the problem and run the command again; completed steps can be repeated safely
- **Exit code:** 5

## GL1013

- **Message:** an NVIDIA GPU is present but greenlens-nvml is not installed
- **Cause:** the helper that reads NVML was not found in `{dirs}`
- **Fix:** install greenlens-nvml from the same release next to greenlens, or set sources.nvml.helper; until then nvidia-smi is used if present
- **Exit code:** 3

## GL1014

- **Message:** the NVIDIA Management Library cannot be used
- **Cause:** `{detail}`
- **Fix:** check that the NVIDIA driver is loaded and that 'nvidia-smi' works for the user of the agent
- **Exit code:** 3

## GL1015

- **Message:** nvidia-smi cannot read the NVIDIA GPUs
- **Cause:** `{detail}`
- **Fix:** check that the NVIDIA driver is loaded and that 'nvidia-smi' works for the user of the agent
- **Exit code:** 3

## GL3001

- **Message:** configuration file not found
- **Cause:** `{path}` does not exist
- **Fix:** check the path given with --config
- **Exit code:** 6

## GL3002

- **Message:** cannot read the configuration file
- **Cause:** `{path}`: `{detail}`
- **Fix:** correct the file; 'greenlens config validate' lists every problem
- **Exit code:** 6

## GL3003

- **Message:** invalid configuration value for `{key}`
- **Cause:** `{detail}`
- **Fix:** see the configuration reference, or run 'greenlens config show' for the values in effect
- **Exit code:** 6

## GL3004

- **Message:** invalid value in the environment variable `{name}`
- **Cause:** `{detail}`
- **Fix:** correct or unset the variable
- **Exit code:** 6

## GL4001

- **Message:** the agent is not running
- **Cause:** cannot connect to `{socket}`: `{detail}`
- **Fix:** start it with 'sudo systemctl start greenlens' or run 'greenlens agent' in another terminal
- **Exit code:** 1

## GL4002

- **Message:** cannot open the database
- **Cause:** `{path}`: `{detail}`
- **Fix:** check that agent.data_dir exists and is writable by the user of the agent
- **Exit code:** 1

## GL4003

- **Message:** cannot create the agent socket
- **Cause:** `{path}`: `{detail}`
- **Fix:** check agent.socket and the permissions of its directory
- **Exit code:** 1

## GL4004

- **Message:** there is no directory for the agent socket
- **Cause:** XDG_RUNTIME_DIR is not set and agent.socket is empty
- **Fix:** set agent.socket in the configuration
- **Exit code:** 6

## GL4005

- **Message:** another agent is already running
- **Cause:** `{path}` accepts connections
- **Fix:** stop the other agent, or give this one a different agent.socket and agent.data_dir
- **Exit code:** 1

## GL4006

- **Message:** the agent rejected the request
- **Cause:** `{status}`: `{detail}`
- **Fix:** check the agent logs, for example with 'journalctl -u greenlens'
- **Exit code:** 1
